what_constrained: Native Pebble resolution and a stale shared Gabbro emulator state complicated visual comparison.
what_worked: Rebuilding the fish with polygons, capturing both targets, and independent screenshot review produced a credible local preview.
what_differently: Prototype scene density at actual watch size earlier; kelp remains sparse.

what_constrained: The 200x228 and 260x260 native screens leave little room for detailed aquarium art around large readable time digits.
what_worked: Checking every scene at native size revealed sparse kelp and reef areas; wider leaves and larger coral/rock silhouettes made the illustration more legible.
what_differently: Confirm the visual direction before starting a new scene pass and reserve physical motion verification before any release.

what_constrained: The original visual target was rich pixel art, and Gabbro could not decode the most detailed castle PNG beside the fish sprite.
what_worked: Recovered the exact concept references, generated native palette assets, inspected both emulator targets, and used an independent review to catch the castle fallback.
what_differently: Budget PNG decode memory during the first native asset study and inspect the first cold-launch frame for each target.

what_constrained: Fish and background choices had been coupled through one scene setting, and round-screen edges could clip small creatures.
what_worked: Preserving the scene as a base preset, testing day-based selection in host C, and reviewing mixed native captures on both targets kept customization readable.
what_differently: Place foreground critters within the round safe area in the first composition pass.

what_constrained: A richer aquarium needed visible life without constant redraws, while mirrored fish art could not mirror the live time or battery label.
what_worked: Short level-based bursts, mirrored sprite resources with upright live text, a brighter blue source, and native left/right captures made the feature reviewable on both targets.
what_differently: Test migration on an existing physical install and measure battery impact before treating motion as release-ready.

what_constrained: Clockfish had no existing RePebble entry, and the store requires platform-specific media at exact native dimensions.
what_worked: Prepared one GIF and four native screenshots for each device, uploaded the reviewed dual-target PBW, then checked the public listing in both device views with a fresh verifier.
what_differently: Capture coordinated motion frames and store media as part of the native build workflow before opening the submission form.

what_constrained: A lively aquarium risked distracting repeated three-second wrist glances, and emulator frames cannot establish comfort or battery impact on a physical watch.
what_worked: Modeled glance overlap before changing timing, constrained fish travel, inspected native glide sequences on both targets, and checked the published 0.7.1 galleries.
what_differently: Test the released motion on both physical watch shapes and measure real battery behavior before claiming it feels natural to wear.

what_constrained: Six built-in font styles had to fit a small fish body on two different screen shapes, and RePebble served old screenshot assets briefly after gallery saves.
what_worked: Capturing 23:58 natively for every style, narrowing the Time 2 bold mapping, testing persistence after emulator restart, and reopening both editor and public listings exposed the real state.
what_differently: Add an explicit screenshot time check to the capture workflow and allow for public media cache propagation before claiming a listing update.
